title: Sandstone Therapeutics — Replatforming Show & Tell: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood API, Console, and Optimize for a replatforming from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Focus: parity map, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/private options, KMS/encryption, rollout strategies. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: cost parity tests, latency benchmark, security questionnaire completion.

transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-11-13
- Start: 16:30 UTC
- Duration: ~76 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM); Tom (Sandstone Eng Manager), Laura (Sandstone SecOps), Evan (Sandstone ML Platform), Maya (Product)

Summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy): Saw console tour, API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together, discussed dedicated vs hosted, KMS and VPC, will run a 2-week pilot.

00:00:03 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this into the week. Quick intro: I’m Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, Priya is our solutions engineer who will drive the technical walkthrough. Diego's here for success and handoffs.
00:00:17 Tom (Sandstone): Thanks Alex, yeah we have a fairly packed agenda. We're replatforming some endpoints off of OpenAI and Anthropic, plus a handful on Together. Hoping to see how straightforward parity will be and, uh, what the operational story looks like.
00:00:31 Priya (Redwood SE): Great. I'll jump into the parity mapping then the console and Optimize suggestions. Quick note — I might share my screen and poke at the runtime traces as we go, sound good?
00:00:40 Maya (Sandstone): Works for me. Also, Laura will want to pause on security bits.
00:00:46 Laura (Sandstone SecOps): Yep. We need to validate KMS, SSO, retention, and evidence for audits — SOC 2 stuff.
00:00:53 Alex: Perfect — we'll cover security and run a checklist at the end.

--- API Parity Mapping (demo) ---
00:01:20 Priya: So first, parity. We mapped your top three endpoints: chat-completion on OpenAI (gpt-4o), Claude-like Anthropic workflows, and a Together generative model used for summarization. On the right is a parity table — model families, tokenization quirks, typical prompt rewrites, and expected output differences.
00:01:44 Evan (Sandstone): Are there any prompt engineering changes needed? Our pipelines do a lot of prompt templating and tool-calling.
00:01:52 Priya: Short answer: minimal. For chat semantics we expose a /chat endpoint that looks very similar to the OpenAI contract. The main differences are model names and some param names — like our temperature tunable and a max_context setting. Example: your Anthropic system prompts map to Redwood system role with a 1:1 recommended rewrite. We included a small snippet that auto-translates role tokens.
00:02:22 Tom: What about streaming and function/tool calling? We rely heavily on streaming token-by-token to the client.
00:02:30 Priya: We support streaming and function calling semantics similar to what you're used to. Small caveat: Together's streaming chunk sizes are a bit different because of their tokenizer; we emulate behavior by adjusting buffer sizes. In practice customers haven't needed to change the client code, just minor buffer-tuning.
00:02:49 Speaker 3: (inaudible)

00:03:10 Priya: Also, we expose per-route fallbacks. If a model variant is overloaded, a route can fallback to a cheaper quantized variant or to a hosted fallback. You can granularly opt-in by endpoint.
00:03:24 Evan: Are those fallbacks instant or do they cause re-requests?
00:03:28 Priya: They’re transparent at the routing layer — the request is routed to a compatible model. There may be a different latency profile, but no client-side retry.

--- Console Tour: Routes, Rollouts, Observability ---
00:04:10 Priya: Switching to Console. This is a demo account view — top nav shows API, Dedicated, Private, and Optimize. Here’s your Routes panel. You can create a route that maps client key + path to a model list, set max tokens, and attach rollout policies.
00:04:32 Maya: Can we restrict routes to certain regions? We need EU-only for some PHI workloads.
00:04:37 Priya: Yes — region selectors per route and you can pin to dedicated pools in eu-west-1.
00:04:42 Laura: And audit logs? We need immutable logs for all token-level calls.
00:04:48 Priya: Audit logs are shipped to your S3/GCS or to our retention store depending on plan. They include request metadata, model, tokens, latency — we can sign and deliver on export windows for audits.
00:05:05 Alex: Quick note — if you plan on Private deployment, logs can remain in your VPC and we never see the payloads.

00:05:32 Priya: Now rollouts. You can create a canary (10%) and auto-increment or roll back based on error rate or quality regression curious — we hook into your eval suite to measure regression automatically if you attach it.
00:05:50 Tom: That eval integration — is that out-of-the-box? We run our own eval harness.
00:05:55 Priya: We support attaching a URL or S3 with your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will run diff checks on output embeddings and similarity thresholds. If you exceed the tolerance, the rollout halts and notifies.
00:06:12 Evan: Does that run per request? Or periodic?
00:06:16 Priya: You can schedule it or trigger it per-rollout. For pilots we usually run it nightly against a snapshot.

--- Optimize: Cost & Performance Toolkit ---
00:06:50 Priya: Now Optimize. This is the section customers find useful when they want to reduce unit cost without sacrificing quality. Onboarded policies include batching recommendations, automatic KV cache suggestions (prefix/persistent caching), and quantization suggestions by model.
00:07:05 Alex: For your summarization model from Together, Optimize suggests int8-quantized variant with a small context-window tweak — that nets ~38% cost reduction in our estimate while keeping ROUGE-ish metrics stable.
00:07:21 Maya: How conservative are those quality estimates? We can’t risk regressions for production meds summaries.
00:07:27 Priya: We attach a confidence band; the Optimize suggestion includes a delta on your eval metric (we ran a sample subset). We can also lock the route to require human approval for any quantized rollout.
00:07:41 Laura: Does quantization impact auditability or KMS?
00:07:44 Priya: No. Quantization happens in the runtime; payloads are still encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are managed by your KMS in private deployments.

--- Security Questions / Private Deployment ---
00:08:10 Laura: Ok, so KMS + data residency — we need to know which keys are visible to Redwood ops in hosted vs private.
00:08:18 Alex: Hosted: keys are managed by Redwood unless you provide a customer-managed key (CMK) via cloud KMS; we have HSM integrations for enterprise. Private: keys never leave your control; logs and keys are in your VPC.
00:08:30 Laura: SOC 2 report? And can we get a pen-test summary?
00:08:34 Diego (CSM): We’ll send the SOC 2 Type II and a redacted penetration test summary after the call. I'll add that to the action items.
00:08:44 Tom: How about RBAC and SSO for the console? We have strict least-privilege requirements.
00:08:49 Priya: Console supports SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC — API key scoping by route and read-only dashboards for auditors.

--- Deep-dive: Latency, Batching, KV Cache ---
00:09:30 Priya: Zooming into runtime: We do workload-aware batching which groups short requests into micro-batches while preserving per-request latency SLOs. KV cache: for chat usecases we cache keys per conversation prefix — this cuts repeated token costs for long sessions.
00:09:47 Evan: Our conversation histories can be 10k tokens. How do you manage KV memory?
00:09:52 Priya: We shard the KV cache across GPUs and evict by LRU and TTL. Also we support partial prefix caching where you persist only the last N tokens as a micro-cache. You can control TTL per-route.
00:10:06 Tom: Any difference for Together models? They use a slightly different KV layout.
00:10:10 Priya: We adapt at the loader stage; for Together-style models we re-chunk the KV so lookup semantics are equivalent. There may be a small warm-up latency on first usage.

00:10:40 Alex: Quick interjection — I want to call out cost modeling. We provide a token-level cost breakdown per route in the console and you can attach committed capacity for Dedicated pools which changes unit pricing dramatically.
00:10:54 Maya: Can we preview dedicated pricing for our 24/7 summarization pipeline?
00:10:59 Alex: Yes — we’ll include a committed vs on-demand comparison in the pricing sheet. Action item for me.

--- Real-world migration considerations ---
00:11:40 Priya: On migrations we usually suggest a staged approach: 1) adapter layer to translate request/response minimally, 2) run both providers in shadow mode for a week, 3) run cost/latency benchmarks, 4) cutover route with canary and eval checks.
00:11:58 Tom: Shadowing doubles our token costs though. Any tips?
00:12:02 Priya: Use sample traffic (10%) and synthetic traffic for heavy paths to avoid paying double across all calls. Also Optimize can run simulated workloads to estimate peak tail latencies.

00:12:30 Evan: We're worried about hallucination behavior differences between Anthropic and OpenAI. Can Redwood help us detect quality regressions?
00:12:36 Priya: Yes — we have a regression detector that measures semantic divergence using embeddings and task-specific metrics. We flag high divergence on the rollout dashboard and can auto-rollback.

--- Customer Questions and Clarifications ---
00:13:10 Laura: We have a compliance window for data retention of 7 years for some records. Does Redwood support long retention and legal hold?
00:13:19 Diego: In Private deployments yes. In hosted we can extend retention on contract and set legal holds + export options.

00:13:40 Tom: How long does an on-prem/private deployment take to stand up? We may need an air-gapped option for a subset of workloads.
00:13:47 Alex: Typical VPC/private control-plane deployments are 4-8 weeks depending on networking approvals. Air-gapped on-prem can be longer — we’ll scope that in the pilot prep.

00:14:10 Maya: What kind of telemetry do we get during the pilot? We want per-token cost, tail-latency percentiles, and model drift metrics.
00:14:17 Priya: Console exports all of that. We'll give you a dashboard and a data export. You can also attach tracing hooks into your existing SRE stack.

00:14:44 Priya: Okay, switching to a short live demo — I’ll show a parity example: a Together summarization request rewritten to Redwood chat endpoint.
00:14:56 [screen share noise]
00:15:10 Priya: Here’s the original curl to Together: curl -X POST https://api.together.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'. And here's the Redwood translation: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"together-summ-1q","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a summarizer"}, ...]}' /v1/chat.
00:15:32 Evan: Looks straightforward. Where would we place the adapter — service side or client side?
00:15:36 Priya: Service side. We recommend a tiny adapter lambda or sidecar that rewrites headers and maps params so you can keep clients intact.

00:15:58 Priya: Demo: console route attached to three model variants — full float, int8-quantized, and a cheaper fallback. I'll trigger a canary to 10%.
00:16:10 [mouse click sounds]
00:16:20 Priya: Canary created, and the rollout is hooked to your eval S3. We'll watch for divergence.
00:16:30 Maya: If the canary fails, what alerts do we get?
00:16:33 Priya: Slack, email, and webhook. Also an auto-rollback if configured.

00:16:55 Tom: On the subject of cost — what kind of per-token delta should we expect when switching Together summarization to int8 on Redwood vs Together hosted?
00:17:03 Alex: Rough ballpark depends on sequence lengths, but we estimated ~30–45% unit cost reduction on the sample set Priya ran. We'll include the raw traces in the benchmark.

--- Technical Nudges & Bugs (transcription noisy) ---
00:17:40 Priya: A couple of gotchas: 1) tokenization differences — sometimes you see a +1 token overhead moving between tokenizers; 2) early stop behavior differs, so we recommend normalizing stop tokens in the adapter; 3) Together model AVX flags on older CPUs can affect local cost estimates.
00:18:02 Evan: For our on-prem infra, GPU packing and fragmentation have been a pain. Does Redwood Dedicated help?
00:18:08 Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved pools and more predictable scheduling. You can configure burst capacity, preemptible instances, and autoscale policies to reduce fragmentation.

00:18:40 Laura: One more compliance nit — do you keep raw prompts in logs? We sometimes need to redact PII from saved records.
00:18:47 Alex: Logged payloads are configurable; you can redact or hash prompts before they land in retention storage. For private deployments, redaction can occur inside your VPC.

00:19:10 Tom: OKay, what's the recommended pilot definition so we can get procurement moving? We need clear success criteria.
00:19:18 Alex: Recommended pilot: 2 weeks, include 3 representative endpoints (chat summary, fine-tuned Q&A, reranking), target 10k tokens/day sample, measure cost delta, 95th percentile latency, and quality parity measured by your eval harness. Success criteria: cost reduction >=20% OR latency improvement >=10% with no quality regression >2% on your primary metric.
00:19:42 Maya: That seems reasonable. We'll need the pricing sheet for committed capacity if the numbers are good.

00:19:58 Priya: I'll create a sample pilot runbook after the call — steps, data URLs, who does shadowing, traffic knobs, and dashboards.

--- Wrap-up & Recap ---
00:20:30 Alex: Quick recap: Redwood will send cost-parity spreadsheet, SOC2 & pen-test docs, and a pilot runbook. Sandstone will identify the 3 endpoints and give us the eval prompt set. We'll aim to kick off the pilot next week pending procurement.
00:20:47 Laura: I'll start the security questionnaire and follow up with Diego.
00:20:50 Tom: Thanks everyone.
00:20:53 Priya: Thanks all — we'll email the materials in the next 24 hours.
00:21:00 [call continues with side conversations about procurement language and scheduling]
01:05:10 Diego: Adding final note — we recorded the call and I'll drop the recording and notes in the CRP. Also, Alex will follow up with a proposed pilot timeline.
01:05:25 Alex: Yep, will do.
01:05:30 Maya: Thanks, bye.
01:05:35 [call ends]
